title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addresses IAS Officer Tainees of 2024 batch at LBSNAA,Mussoorie
subtitle:
Civil servants are the vital link in translating the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 into reality: Vice-President
Vice-President urges IAS officers to prioritise team excellence, integrity and citizen-centric governance
“Make Seva bhav and Kartavya bodh your guiding mantra”: Vice-President
“True leadership is not measured by power or position, but by the ability to act ethically”: Vice-President
Technology, continuous learning and adaptability essential for future-ready civil services: Vice-President
body_text:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Valedictory Programme of Phase-II training of the IAS Officer Trainees of the 2024 batch at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA), Mussoorie.

Radhakrishnan today addressed the Valedictory Programme of Phase-II training of the IAS Officer Trainees of the 2024 batch at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration (LBSNAA), Mussoorie. The Vice-President said that civil services… pic.twitter.com/lMRuNcIomv — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 20, 2026
Congratulating the Officer Trainees on the successful completion of their training, the Vice-President said that civil services have made immense contributions to the country’s development and remain a vital link between policy and its implementation at the grassroots level. Referring to the journey towards Viksit Bharat @ 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged the officers to ensure that development reaches the last mile and is inclusive. He called upon them to make “Sevabhav and Kartavyabodh” their guiding mantra. Emphasising teamwork, the Vice-President urged the young officers to strive for team excellence rather than individual or group excellence. He stressed the importance of building cohesive teams, motivating colleagues and carrying forward good practices established by their predecessors. Highlighting the increasing representation of women in civil services, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan noted that around 41 per cent of the 2024 batch are women. He described this progress as a powerful testament to Nari Shakti, where talent rises above stereotypes and determination overcomes obstacles. The Vice-President also called upon the officers to embrace emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning and Blockchain, to improve efficiency, transparency and citizen service delivery. He emphasised continuous learning, adaptability and being future-ready. Stressing that character and integrity are the foundations of public service, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that true leadership is not measured by power or position, but by the ability to act ethically even in difficult situations. Concluding his address, the Vice-President urged the officers to make their service meaningful by transforming lives in the remotest corners of the country and ensuring that every grievance is heard and every citizen is empowered. Governor of Uttarakhand, Lieutenant General (Retd.) Gurmit Singh; Minister of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Soldier Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand, Shri Ganesh Joshi; Director, LBSNAA, Dr. B. Rajender were present during the occasion.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and former Prime Minister Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri at LBSNAA, Mussoorie today. pic.twitter.com/NOlqw5RSGh — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) August 20, 2026

enrichment.summary: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Valedictory Programme of Phase-II training for the 2024 batch of IAS Officer Trainees at LBSNAA, Mussoorie. He urged officers to prioritise teamwork, integrity, citizen-centric governance, and adoption of emerging technologies like AI and blockchain. He also noted that around 41% of the 2024 batch are women, calling it a testament to Nari Shakti.
enrichment.context: This is a routine ceremonial address by the Vice-President at LBSNAA, a recurring event marking the completion of training phases for IAS probationers. Such speeches typically reiterate values of ethical leadership, service orientation, and administrative efficiency without announcing new policy, schemes, or institutional changes. The mention of rising female representation in the civil services reflects an ongoing, gradual trend rather than a new development.
